title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery: Rates After a Recent Veterans Pension Rate Adjustment
content:
A recent cut in a debtor's **Veterans Pension** rate sets a rate-cut rate when the lump sum of a compromise offer on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** is measured.

**Rule.** When the debtor's pension rate was adjusted in the last twelve calendar months by an adjustment that created an overpayment, the overpaid rate-cut rate of 85 percent applies. When it was adjusted in that period without creating an overpayment, the plain rate-cut rate of 95 percent applies. Otherwise no rate-cut rate applies.

**Reading the records.** The rate adjustments are those recorded in the debtor's Veterans Pension records, each dated and marked as having created an overpayment or not. Where both kinds fall in the period, an adjustment that created an overpayment decides the rate. A period of so many calendar months counted back from today covers the dates from which fewer than that many whole calendar months have passed to today: on 20 October, the last six months include 21 April but not 20 April. The rate-cut rate is a percentage of the recovery remaining after the cost deduction, acting on that one figure before the limit to the balance and the final rounding.

| Pension rate adjustment in the last twelve months | Rate-cut rate |
|---|---|
| At least one that created an overpayment | 85 percent |
| Only adjustments that created none | 95 percent |
| None | None |

**Hypothetical case.** A figure of 4,000.00 USD with a pension rate adjustment eight months ago that created an overpayment: 3,400.00 USD.
